title: Champions of Norrath
subtitle: Enter Norrath with a smaller party
summary: Champions of Norrath is Snowblind Studios' PlayStation 2 action role-playing game, first released in North America on 10 February 2004. Set in the EverQuest universe, it gives a single player or a cooperative group a direct journey through forests, settlements and dungeons. Choosing a character begins a cycle of fighting, gathering equipment and improving abilities. The world supplies a larger fantasy setting without requiring the player to join the online role-playing game from which it came. Its adventure is organised around a small party moving together towards the next encounter.
body: Champions of Norrath is Snowblind Studios' PlayStation 2 action role-playing game, first released in North America on 10 February 2004. Set in the EverQuest universe, it gives a single player or a cooperative group a direct journey through forests, settlements and dungeons. Choosing a character begins a cycle of fighting, gathering equipment and improving abilities. The world supplies a larger fantasy setting without requiring the player to join the online role-playing game from which it came. Its adventure is organised around a small party moving together towards the next encounter.

A character's race, appearance and abilities establish the starting point, while experience and discovered equipment guide later development. Monsters leave rewards that make the next stretch of the journey more manageable, connecting exploration to practical improvement. Different party members can contribute different strengths during cooperative play. The player therefore considers both the next useful item and how the group works when several threats arrive together. A familiar dungeon becomes a place to search carefully because the contents can change what a character is capable of doing afterwards.

The game expands the technology used for Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance, carrying Snowblind's console action-role-playing approach into Norrath. Up to four players can cooperate, with the PlayStation 2 Network Adapter originally enabling online groups as well as local play. Inon Zur composed the music. Ubisoft published the European edition in June 2004, and Champions: Return to Arms followed in 2005. The original's appeal is straightforward and durable: a party enters a dangerous place together, emerges with better equipment and immediately has another reason to see what lies beyond it.
